To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quality of decisions about cancer treatments can be improved by increasing patients’ knowledge, matching patients’ preferences with treatments, and improving the quality of information provided by clinicians.
the quality of decision-making in cancer care can be improved by providing information to patients and clinicians, and by helping patients and clinicians to understand the preferences of patients.
there is considerable evidence that cancer care is not always of high quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality of decision-making in cancer care, and we propose a framework to guide the design of interventions to improve decision quality.
the quality of the decision-making process in cancer care.
the development and evaluation of systems to improve the quality and outcomes of cancer care.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
systems support is needed to help patients and their providers make the right decisions about cancer care.

the quality of cancer decision making could be improved by the development of a system that supports patients in making decisions that are consistent with their values and preferences and that is supported by evidence.
systems support is necessary for improving the quality and efficiency of cancer care decisions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
“doing the right thing” is a complex problem and that systems are needed to support the quality of cancer decisions.
the best way to improve the quality in cancer care is to improve decisions.
“doing the right thing is not enough; systems support is needed to ensure that the right thing is done.”
The main takeaway from our work is that
the strategies to support decision quality in cancer need to be customized to the specific decision being made.
there are a variety of decision types in cancer and the appropriate strategies to improve decision making differ.
the appropriate system support for improving the decision quality depends on the type of decision.
